row.scenario: Your agent gets a full virtual machine with its own kernel, root and a public address, and can be reinstalled from your own ISO.
row.note: A real virtual machine, not a container: you can install any of the Linux templates or boot your own ISO, enable a routed /64 of IPv6, join a private VLAN and reboot without touching anyone else. HostHatch's pages call them VMs and never name the hypervisor, here or in the docs. The 2, 4 and 8 GB plans are fair-share CPU, so the entry price does not buy dedicated cores.

source.quote: You can also upload your own ISO image using our control panel, and deploy it on your VMs with us, just like you would on a bare-metal or a physical server.

row.scenario: You pick one of ten fixed plans in one of the advertised locations; CPU and memory only change by moving to another plan.
row.note: Ten compute plans from 1 core / 2 GB / 10 GB to 16 cores / 96 GB / 250 GB, plus storage VMs to 10 TB. CPU and memory are fixed bundles, so there is no 3-core / 6 GB machine; an upgrade moves the server to another plan and a reboot applies it. The location count is inconsistent: the product page says 16, the documentation matrix lists 14 cities, and the status page monitors 13. Madrid, Milan and Warsaw appear in the site's product data but not in the docs; Seoul appears in the docs but not in the product data.

row.scenario: You can stop, start, reboot and reinstall the server, but a stop is a power-off: memory and running processes are gone and the paid term still bills.
row.note: The API has power-on, shutdown, power-off, reboot and reinstall actions. A stop keeps the disk and its files but loses RAM and every running process; there is no pause, hibernate or fork. The contract is a monthly or longer term that renews until cancelled, and a cancellation set to end_of_term keeps the server 'until the end of the period you paid for', so powering off never reduces the bill.

source.quote: The term of this Agreement shall begin upon the date the server is installed and made available to customer and shall be for 1 month (or any other billing period selected by the customer) and shall renew for the same successive terms until terminated

row.scenario: You can snapshot a server's disk, restore it onto any server in the project, or order a new server from it — but not capture a running process or fork a live machine.
row.note: A snapshot is a copy of the disk, taken on demand, kept until deleted and owned by the project rather than the server. It can be restored onto another server in the project, or used instead of an image when ordering a new one, which is the closest thing to a template. There is no memory snapshot and no live fork. The account's snapshot limit is not published, snapshots have no published price, and automated backups are not sold: a 2023 'upcoming features' block promised them but they appear nowhere in the current docs, API or panel.

source.quote: A snapshot is a copy of a server's disk at one moment.

row.scenario: Files sit on local NVMe and survive a stop; a separate storage line goes to 10 TB, but nothing detaches from the server or outlives it.
row.note: Compute plans carry 10–250 GB of local NVMe and storage plans 1–10 TB of RAID-10 HDD with 1–2 cores and 1–2 GB of RAM. Disk survives a stop and can grow on an upgrade, but it is tied to the server: there is no detachable block volume, no shared volume and no object storage. The 2023 features page still lists block storage as 'upcoming'; it does not exist in the current API or product list. Backups are not sold, so the copy that outlives the server is your own.

source.quote: our storage VMs are designed for massive storage capacity, scalable up to hundreds of terabytes

row.figure: No idle stop or session cap
row.scenario: Nothing puts the server to sleep: an agent that waits all day keeps its process, its connection and its address.
row.note: The only server states are running, stopped and suspended, and the only power actions are on, shutdown, power off, reboot and reinstall. No idle timer, automatic sleep, wake trigger or maximum session length appears in the API, the documentation or the panel, so an always-on Hermes agent, bot gateway or MCP server can run for the whole term. The trade is that idle hours bill like busy ones, and there is no provider-side scheduler: recurring work runs from cron inside the guest.

row.scenario: The server answers on its own public IPv4 with real SSH, a VNC or serial console in the panel, a routed /64 of IPv6 and any TCP port you open.
row.note: Every server gets a primary public IPv4 and can enable a routed /64 of IPv6; SSH is a normal daemon, so any TCP or UDP service is reachable once the firewall allows it. The panel has a VNC and a serial console for when SSH fails. There is no private or tokenised URL, no provider tunnel and no managed reverse proxy — those are yours to build.

source.quote: We support both dynamic (DHCP) and static IPv4 configuration.

row.scenario: Point an A record at the server and you are reachable; the certificate and its renewal are yours to run.
row.note: HostHatch does not sell DNS hosting or certificates for a VPS. The API manages reverse DNS only, so a custom domain means an A or AAAA record at your own DNS provider plus a reverse proxy and certificate inside the guest. The fixed public IPv4 makes the record easy to keep pointed at the machine, and the routed /64 gives you IPv6 for free.

source.quote: We support both dynamic (DHCP) and static IPv4 configuration.

row.scenario: Outbound data is included up to the plan's monthly allowance, extra is $4 a TB, and egress can be restricted with firewall rules.
row.note: Each plan includes 1–20 TB a month with inbound and outbound counted together, reset on the 1st of the calendar month; APAC allowances are lower (500 GB on the 2 GB plan in Hong Kong, Tokyo, Sydney and Singapore). When the allowance is used the server is rate-limited to 5 Mbps rather than billed automatically; more transfer is $4 per TB through support. Firewall groups can be created with an egress direction, so you can allow only named destinations or block outbound entirely. The primary IPv4 is static for the life of the server, and BYOIP with BGP is available.

source.quote: Additional bandwidth can be added for $4 per TB by contacting our support.

row.scenario: API keys can be read-only and can expire, but there is no secret store and nothing hides a model key from an agent running as root.
row.note: API keys are created on the profile page, can be read-only, can be given an expiry date and are revoked when the password changes. A key is not limited to one project: it carries your access to every project you belong to, and project roles (member, admin, owner) decide what it may do there. SSH keys are stored per project and installed at order. There is no secrets manager and no request-signing proxy, so a credential the agent needs sits in a file the agent can read.

source.quote: A key carries your access to every project you belong to.

row.scenario: You can create, power, reinstall, snapshot and firewall servers from the panel or from a documented REST API with an OpenAPI document.
row.note: The API at console.hosthatch.com/api/v1 covers projects, servers, power actions, reinstall, root-password reset, snapshots, ISOs, firewalls, SSH keys, reverse DNS and orders, with idempotency keys, stable error codes, read-only keys and an OpenAPI document. There is no official CLI, Python or TypeScript SDK, no MCP server, and no PTY or file-transfer endpoint. Cloud-init user data is documented but answers feature_unavailable, and ISO upload through the API is not available yet (the panel can upload one).

source.quote: The HostHatch API lets your code, scripts and AI agents do what you do in the console: order servers and pay for them with account credit, power and reinstall them, take snapshots, set up firewalls, mount ISOs, and manage SSH keys and reverse DNS.

row.scenario: You get a bare operating system and install the agent yourself; there is no template, no prompt API and no built-in browser.
row.note: The order flow offers Linux distribution images and your own ISO, nothing else. There is no Hermes, OpenClaw, n8n or Docker template, no coding agent in any image, no prompt endpoint, no hosted browser and no managed desktop. A graphical desktop can be installed from an ISO and watched through the VNC console, but that is your install, not a product.

source.quote: We offer pre-ready cloud templates for the major Linux distributions.

row.scenario: A small team can share projects with owner, admin and member roles, but there is no single sign-on, no audit log and no hard spending cap.
row.note: Servers, snapshots, keys, firewalls, ISOs and orders live in projects, and each person has one of three roles in each project; the project owner's account credit pays for every order. Read-only API keys and password-plus-2FA sign-in exist. What is missing for a company: SAML or OIDC single sign-on, an audit log of who changed what, and any account-wide cap that stops another server being ordered.

source.quote: A project holds servers, SSH keys, firewall groups, snapshots, ISOs, actions and orders, and the people who manage them.

row.scenario: A long-running independent host with its own network and hardware, but no uptime promise and a thin public paper trail for a cautious buyer.
row.note: HostHatch LLC has traded since around 2011, is privately funded, runs its own equipment and its own ARIN-registered network (AS63473), and publishes a status page (99.994% over 90 days on 2026-11-04) and a GDPR DPA. It publishes no SLA: the terms contain no uptime percentage or credit schedule, only a pro-rata refund for an interruption caused solely by its breach of warranty. Support is by ticket, its own promotional post warns that replies can take days on promotional plans, Trustpilot showed 2.7 from 93 reviews, and there is no SOC 2 report or ISO 27001 certificate on the site.

source.quote: HostHatch warrants that the Service(s) shall be provided in a workmanlike and professional manner.

row.scenario: A flat monthly plan is the only meter: a box that mostly waits costs the same as one that works, and a short task costs a whole month.
row.note: One prepaid plan per server, $4 to $69 a month for compute and $5 to $38 for storage. The terms invoice monthly, quarterly, semi-annually or annually, but there is no hourly or per-second rate and no cheaper stopped rate. The published monthly price is used in this guide because the checkout's longer-term prices are behind the login. Promotional plans sold through LowEndTalk are annual or three-year prepay only, limited stock, non-refundable and slower to set up.

source.quote: HostHatch will invoice Customer for Fees and Expenses monthly, quarterly, semi-annually or annually.

row.scenario: There is no free tier and no starting credit; you pay the first invoice before the server exists and can ask for the money back within seven days only if the fault is HostHatch's.
row.note: No free plan, trial credit or free sandbox hours appear on the product page, the signup page or the terms. The only safety net is a 7-day money-back guarantee that requires a valid reason caused by HostHatch and evidence in a ticket; used resources may be deducted, and upgrades, setup fees and all non-VPS services are excluded. The payment methods accepted at signup are not published.

source.quote: Our virtual private servers (VPS) carry a 7-day money back guarantee with a valid reason requirement.
